hills.description: The new program uses a multi-resolution approach: it starts from a resampled grid and applies block-multiplicative perturbations, edge-preserving smoothing, and global noise, rather than the record's single-resolution coordinate hill climb with a final line search. It also uses a fixed random seed and a 90% CPU deadline with a different perturbation mix (blocks, smoothing, noise) instead of the r…

This program optimises a smooth soft-max surrogate of the sup-norm (log-sum-exp with increasing sharpness β) via L-BFGS on a squared-parameterisation w↦w², rather than hill-climbing heights directly. It adds Anderson extrapolation on the fixed-point iteration to accelerate convergence, and it anneals β across three stages with repeated rounds per stage. It also seeds from several sine-power bumps…

This program optimises the full autocorrelation ratio directly via Dinkelbach iterations on a square-root variable with a soft-max surrogate for the infinity norm, rather than isolating the level-transition loss and perturbing along its gradient. Instead of gradient-guided perturbations, it explores by rank-ordering cells, zeroing or rescaling contiguous runs of the lowest 15% of heights, and zer…

This program seeds a hand-built spike-plus-decaying-comb shape and refines it with a Dinkelbach-style ascent that maximizes num − λ·l1·linf via random contiguous-block scaling, rather than starting from the record's symmetric construction and moving f along the transition-loss gradient. Its move loop is two-sided and multi-scale, scaling bottom-15% runs down/zero and top-30% runs up, with periodi…

This program optimises a smooth soft-max surrogate of the sup-norm (exponential penalty with β annealed 500→2000→8000) via Dinkelbach iterations on a squared-weight parametrisation, rather than perturbing along a transition-loss gradient with shallow re-polishing. axes.name: How is a candidate solution represented?

values.name: a fixed-length dense real vector of length 50 (np.ones(50))
a piecewise-constant function on a nonuniform adaptive grid with variable breakpoints
a parametric family (e.g. Gaussian mixture / spline coefficients) with few parameters
variable-length dense vector with resampling between resolutions
a nonnegative height vector on a fixed uniform grid, convolved with itself
a parametric family (e.g. spline/Gaussian-mixture coefficients) optimised in a low-dimensional space
a signed or complex-valued function, or one defined on an irregular/adaptive grid
nonnegative real heights on a fixed uniform grid, with the grid resolution fixed (n=4000/8000/50000) and f constrained to be nonnegative
allow signed f (negative heights), which changes the autocorrelation structure entirely
use a non-uniform / adaptive grid or a parametric shape (splines, few-parameter bumps) instead of per-cell heights

axes.name: How is the first solution built?

values.name: return start unchanged if given, else a constant
use start as a seed and locally perturb/optimize it
ignore start and always construct from scratch
a smooth analytic bump (sine-power) or the upsampled previous best
random multi-start over many random initial vectors
start from a known extremal shape (e.g. indicator/step or triangular) and deform
a smooth analytic seed (sine-power bump, or the record's symmetric construction, or a hand-built spike-plus-comb) then local ascent
start from random sparse / heavy-tailed noise and let the search discover structure
start from a completely different combinatorial construction (e.g. a difference set / Sidon-like sequence)

axes.name: What quantity does the search optimise while it runs?

values.name: Dinkelbach surrogate A - lambda*L1*LSE
exact ratio R with exact argmax gradient

axes.name: Which moves or update steps change a solution?

values.name: L-BFGS-B steps on w=sqrt(f)
multiplicative coordinate descent on h
projected gradient ascent with adaptive step
projected gradient ascent on h
contiguous-run operations: scale/zero bottom-percentile runs, transfer mass between runs, warp windows, block scaling
non-contiguous / scattered single-cell edits or random subset mutations
global parametric transforms (resample, Fourier-domain filtering, convolution with a kernel) applied to the whole f

axes.name: How does the search accept worse solutions or escape a local optimum?

values.name: anneal beta and keep best R
random multiplicative restarts and coordinate line search
random kicks on stalled gradient ascent
strict improvement of R (accept only if r_new > cur_R + tiny epsilon), i.e. monotone hill climbing
allow worsening moves with a temperature / tabu schedule (simulated annealing) to escape basins
maintain a population and accept by diversity or novelty rather than by R alone

axes.name: How is the problem's scale handled (all at once, coarse to fine, in parts)?

values.name: fixed resolution chosen up front (optionally one doubling), tuned by hand
continuously refine resolution as a function of remaining budget (multigrid)
optimise at coarse resolution then interpolate and re-optimise adaptively

axes.name: Which parts, if any, are solved exactly?
How is the time budget split between phases?

values.name: ignored entirely; no time-aware search or evaluation
allocate budget across a coarse-to-fine multiscale search
use budget for a stochastic optimizer (simulated annealing / CMA-ES) with restarts
a fixed step-size schedule or fixed iteration count with a CPU-deadline guard
adaptive step sizes from a line search or trust region on the ratio
budget allocated by a bandit/portfolio across several search strategies
a single CPU-time deadline with a fixed phase split (e.g. ~95s phase A then move loop until deadline-10s), one process
many short independent restarts with different seeds and keep the best
population / island model running several candidate shapes in parallel and recombining

axes.name: How is the ratio R optimised: the objective the optimiser actually works on

values.name: Dinkelbach: maximise ||f*f||_2^2 - lambda*||f*f||_1*smoothmax(f*f), then lambda = R, repeated
Gradient steps on R itself (or log R) with a smooth max
Active-set minimax: the tied maxima of f*f as constraints with dual weights (LP, SLSQP, persistent dual)
Exact line search on R per block or run of f (no gradient)
Alternating projection: push f*f towards a two-level target, then project back to f >= 0
no explicit optimization; relies on a known analytic value (2/3)
directly maximize the ratio via numerical evaluation
optimize a surrogate/smooth relaxation of the ratio
the exact ratio R = ||f*f||_2^2 / (||f*f||_1 ||f*f||_inf) (or a soft-max surrogate of it, annealed to the exact ratio)
optimise a different but related functional (e.g. ||f*f||_2 / ||f*f||_1 alone, or the L2/Linf ratio without the L1 norm…
optimise a multi-objective / Pareto combination (e.g. maximise plateau length subject to a cap on the Linf penalty) rat…

axes.name: How is the maximum of f*f (the L-infinity norm) handled in the optimised objective

values.name: Exact maximum (a subgradient at the arg max)
LogSumExp smooth max normalised by max(f*f), beta annealed upward (1e5 to 1e9 and beyond, up to 1e14)
A fixed mild smooth max (beta about 100-500 relative to the max)
A softmax- or p-norm-weighted set of the top lags
compute ||f*f||_inf exactly as the max of the discrete autocorrelation and divide
optimise a smooth soft-max / log-sum-exp surrogate of the sup-norm with annealing
use a Dinkelbach or minimax reformulation that treats the max as an explicit constraint
treat the argmax of f*f as a single point (exact gradient with indicator at argmax) or a soft-max surrogate annealed to sharpness
explicitly control the plateau: optimise the width of the near-max region of f*f as a first-class objective
use a hard constraint / barrier that keeps f*f flat over a target interval (minimax formulation)

values.name: L-BFGS on smooth surrogate

axes.name: How is f >= 0 enforced

values.name: f = w^2 exactly (a cell at zero stays at zero: the support is locked)
Clip or project to f >= 0 after each step
An explicit support mask pruned on purpose (zero the smallest cells, re-optimise, repeat)

axes.name: How is the number of steps n chosen and changed

values.name: Exact k-fold repeat np.repeat(f, k) (R unchanged), then polish at the finer grid
Zero-pad to the step limit and polish there, letting structure grow into the padding

Coarse to fine, upsampling by interpolation between stages

values.name: One heavy comb block holding about 30% of the mass at one end, an empty gap beside it, a graded ramp of bumps

A smooth arcsine-like density, 1/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) on [-1/2, 1/2]
A parametric series sum_j a_j (1 - 4x^2)^(j - 1/2) (about 100 terms)
Regular sparse packets under a smooth raised-cosine envelope
constant (flat) function
smooth bump / Gaussian-like profile
piecewise-linear or triangular profile with tunable width
sine-power bump seed then optimized

axes.name: What is the fine structure of f (the comb of teeth or blocks)

values.name: A fine, coherent periodic lattice of teeth (period about 0.3% of the domain)
Contiguous blocks with irregular spacing found by optimisation (hundreds to thousands of blocks)
A coarser parent with each cell split into about 20 sub-cells under a phase kernel
Number-theoretic support (Sidon/B2 sets, difference sets, quadratic residues)
Regular [small, big, small] triplets

Gaussian-blurred global noise perturbation
plateau-fill ascent then refine
multi-scale height-smoothing anneal then exact re-polish

axes.name: Which part of f*f does the program's step aim at

values.name: The level transitions of f*f (lags with f*f/max between 0.1 and 0.9)
Only the tied maxima (the active set of the L-infinity norm)
Small-mass runs of f first

compact support with zero padding and tunable width
